## Purpose and scope {#scope}

Pi advisor gives the main agent a separate reasoning partner. The main agent explains the problem and supplies evidence across multiple turns.

The advisor cannot inspect code, run tools, or inherit the parent conversation. The main agent owns investigation, verification, implementation, and authorization.

The user requested a standalone extension, with a specification before implementation. This draft records the initial implementation contract, not separate policy approval.

V1 excludes persistence, restoration, automatic summarization, forks, autonomous consultation loops, workspace collection, custom providers, and a dependency on pi-magic8ball.

## Design and implementation choices {#design}

Use one process-local consultation manager per extension instance. Call the host model registry directly with an explicit tool-free context. Do not create a nested Pi agent runtime.

Consultations remain available across parent turns and compaction. Clear them on session start, tree navigation, and shutdown. Switch, fork, and reload replace the runtime. Do not restore consultations from tool results.

The extension writes no consultation files. Pi can still persist tool arguments and results in its parent transcript. The configured provider receives explicit consultation messages. Ephemeral means no separate extension persistence, not guaranteed erasure by Pi or the provider.

REQ-31 removes the fixed consultation, exchange, message-byte, reply-byte, and output-token caps at the user's request.
REQ-29 retains the pinned model context window. REQ-26 retains the configurable deadline, with a 300000 ms default.
Pi controls the model output allowance. Settings-file and presentation bounds remain separate from consultation capacity.
These controls do not provide a monetary guarantee.

Settings use the host agent directory, not a hard-coded home path. Project settings require current Pi project trust. No default model is selected. No live provider calls are part of build verification.

## Tool and lifecycle contract {#contract}

<a id="REQ-1"></a>

**REQ-1** Isolated multi-turn consultation

The extension MUST expose advisor({message, session?}). Omitted session starts a new consultation. Present session continues only that consultation.
Message MUST be a nonblank string. Session MUST be a nonempty opaque identifier when present. Null and unknown fields MUST fail validation.
On successful creation, the extension MUST pin the explicitly configured physical chat model. Continuations MUST use that selection despite later configuration changes.
Every model request MUST contain only the fixed advisor system prompt and that consultation's explicit exchanges. It MUST declare zero tools.
The extension MUST NOT read parent messages, instructions, source files, environment model selections, or another consultation's exchanges into the request.


<a id="REQ-2"></a>

**REQ-2** Advice and output protocol

The advisor prompt MUST distinguish reported observations, interpretations, assumptions, and hypotheses. It MUST permit questions and challenges to the main agent's framing.
The prompt MUST state that advice is not evidence or authorization. It MUST ask the main agent to gather missing evidence.
REQ-17 defines the unstructured reply contract and replaces the former marker and status requirements.
Tool calls, nontext/nonthinking blocks, and non-stop completion reasons MUST fail.
Thinking content MUST NOT enter the returned response or retained transcript. Advice MUST NOT close the consultation or grant permission to act.


<a id="REQ-3"></a>

**REQ-3** Atomic exchanges and failures

Each advisor call MUST make at most one model request. Provider retries MUST be disabled. Automatic fallback MUST NOT occur.
Only a validated reply MUST commit its user/reply pair. Failed creation MUST leave no consultation. Failed continuation MUST preserve previous exchanges.
The extension MUST combine caller cancellation with the deadline defined by REQ-26, measured from call entry. Cancellation MUST prevent a later commit.
Timeout and cancellation MUST return without waiting indefinitely for a provider that ignores abort. Late completions MUST NOT change state.
Concurrent calls on one consultation MUST reject the second with busy. Different consultations MAY run concurrently. REQ-31 removes the active consultation cap.
Failures MUST use fixed safe error codes and messages. Raw provider exceptions MUST NOT appear in output.
Results MUST report usage available at return, including rejected completed replies. Usage from a late unobserved completion MAY be unavailable.


<a id="REQ-4"></a>

**REQ-4** Resource limits

The extension MUST enforce inclusive hard limits: 8 active consultations, 24 committed exchange pairs per consultation, and 16384 UTF-8 bytes per message or raw reply text.
Retained transcript bytes MUST equal the UTF-8 size of JSON.stringify([{role,text}, ...]) and MUST NOT exceed 49152 bytes.
The pending user entry MUST pass byte validation before model work. The full pair MUST pass validation before commit.
A request MUST specify maxTokens = 4096. Token limits remain subject to provider support. Byte and turn limits MUST hold locally.
Crossing a limit MUST return limit-exceeded without changing the prior transcript. The extension MUST NOT evict, trim, compact, or summarize implicitly.
Closed consultations MUST release their slot. Limits reset for a new consultation or a cleared parent lifecycle.


<a id="REQ-5"></a>

**REQ-5** Discovery, close, and reset

advisor_sessions({}) MUST return metadata without full transcripts. REQ-13 defines the fields in addition to session, label, turns, model, and busy.
Label MUST derive from the first explicit message, collapse whitespace, and contain at most 80 Unicode code points. No full transcript MUST appear.
advisor_close({session}) MUST remove an idle consultation and return its identifier. Unknown identifiers MUST return not-found. Busy close MUST return busy.
A cleared manager MUST abort all pending work and reject late commits. Old identifiers MUST become not-found.
The extension MUST clear state on session_start, session_tree, and session_shutdown. Pi 1.0.4 replaces the runtime on session switch and fork through shutdown/start.
Reload MUST create fresh state. Parent compaction MUST NOT clear consultations. State MUST NOT be reconstructed from persisted entries.


<a id="REQ-17"></a>

**REQ-17** Unstructured advisor text

The advisor prompt MUST request natural-language advice without required markers, JSON, or status labels.
After REQ-16 validation, the extension MUST join text blocks with a newline and return that text unchanged in response. It MUST retain the same text in consultation history. It MUST NOT trim nonblank text, strip marker-looking text, parse advice as JSON, classify advice, or infer a status.
Marker-looking strings, quotations, lists, code fences, and JSON-looking text MUST be ordinary reply content. Their presence, absence, repetition, or placement MUST NOT affect acceptance.
The extension MUST remove status from successful advisor results, session metadata, session state, schemas, and presentation. It MUST NOT substitute a guessed or constant classification field.
Structured tool envelopes MUST remain extension-generated and schema-validated. Model selection, isolation, thinking removal, provider completion validation, byte/turn/session bounds, usage, cancellation, rollback, and no automatic retry MUST remain unchanged.


## Configuration contract {#configuration}

<a id="REQ-6"></a>

**REQ-6** Explicit trusted settings

Settings MUST be strict JSON objects with optional model: {provider, model, reasoning?} and optional root timeoutMs.
REQ-20 defines reasoning. REQ-26 defines timeout validation and independent timeout precedence.
Both identifiers MUST be nonblank strings without control characters or whitespace.
Missing files and {} MUST mean unconfigured. Malformed, oversized, null, or unknown-field settings MUST fail closed.
The extension MUST read <agent-dir>/advisor.json first. Only a trusted project MAY add <cwd>/.pi/advisor.json.
A project model MUST replace the entire global model pair. An empty project object MUST retain the global pair. Invalid global settings MUST fail even with a valid project override.
Reads MUST accept only bounded regular UTF-8 files, at most 16384 bytes. Immediate parent or target symlinks and special files MUST be rejected.
A new consultation MUST fail with not-configured or model-unavailable when selection or authentication is unavailable. Virtual models MUST be rejected.
Normal Pi authentication MUST serve model requests. The extension MUST NOT read credentials or change the parent's active model.


<a id="REQ-7"></a>

**REQ-7** User-only settings command

The extension MUST register /advisor [--global|--project] [show | model <provider> <model> | reasoning [level] | timeout [milliseconds|default]].
Global MUST be the default save scope. REQ-20 and REQ-21 define reasoning commands and argument autocomplete.
In TUI mode, a bare command MUST use the inline searchable picker defined by REQ-10. Other UI modes MUST retain the standard selection dialog.
Without UI, it MUST emit settings and usage as a Pi custom message.
Every non-UI command report MUST use customType advisor-settings, display: true, and triggerTurn: false. No report MUST start a model turn.
show MUST display effective selection and source. Invalid commands or cancelled selection MUST write nothing and call no model.
An explicit pair MUST resolve to a physical chat model before save. Project saves MUST recheck trust.
Saves MUST touch only advisor.json and owned temporary or lock files. They MUST serialize participating writers and acquire an exclusive lock.
Replacement MUST be atomic through a same-directory temporary file. First creation MUST NOT replace a newly appeared file.
At the final comparison, changed bytes or lock contention MUST fail closed. No stale-lock reclamation MUST occur.
Cleanup MUST remove only owned temporary files and locks. A save error MUST warn that a save may have completed and require inspection before retry.


<a id="REQ-10"></a>

**REQ-10** Model picker matches /model

The TUI picker MUST copy the inline interface pattern used by pi-magic8ball and Pi 1.0.4 /model.
It MUST show at most 10 model rows and at most max(1, terminal.rows - 2) total rows. Every rendered line MUST fit its terminal width.
It MUST provide editable fuzzy search across provider, model identifier, and display name, using Pi fuzzyFilter ranking.
Every nonempty query edit MUST select the best match. Text keys, including j and k, MUST edit the input.
Arrow keys MUST wrap through filtered results. The effective configured advisor model MUST appear first before search with a current-selection marker.
When at least 10 total rows fit, the picker MUST show the selected display name and navigation hints.
An empty result set MUST show No matching models. Enter with no match MUST leave the picker open.
Escape and Ctrl+C MUST cancel without settings writes. Focus MUST propagate to the search input for cursor and IME placement.
Navigation and resize MUST keep the selected item visible. Truncation MUST NOT change the model identifier returned or saved.
Non-TUI UI clients MUST retain the existing provider/model selection labels and cancellation behavior.
The picker MUST use the current available physical model snapshot. It MUST NOT generate, change the conversation model, or refresh remote catalogs.


<a id="REQ-20"></a>

**REQ-20** Configured advisor reasoning effort

The model selection MAY contain reasoning: default, off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, or max.
Null, nonstring, unknown, or incorrectly cased values MUST fail settings validation.
Omission and default MUST retain the prior request behavior without inheriting the parent thinking level.
As in pi-magic8ball, off MUST omit the simple-stream reasoning option. It MUST be accepted only when the model advertises off support.
Other explicit levels MUST be forwarded unchanged on every advisor request. The model and reasoning selection MUST remain pinned per consultation.
The extension MUST check explicit levels against Pi getSupportedThinkingLevels plus default before each provider request.
Unsupported levels MUST return unsupported-reasoning without generation, retry, clamping, or model fallback.
The user-only reasoning command without a level MUST report effective selection, configured level, and supported choices without writes or generation.
A reasoning <level> command MUST save a complete model selection through the existing atomic writer and trust checks.
Global writes MUST use the global selection, never copy a project override. Trusted project writes MAY copy the effective selection.
Explicit model commands and the picker MUST replace the complete selection. A new selection without reasoning MUST reset effort to legacy behavior.
Successful result and discovery model metadata MUST retain explicit reasoning. Expanded advisor results MUST show the pinned level or legacy default.
Tool input schemas MUST NOT permit caller-supplied reasoning. Thinking removal, unstructured advice, usage, limits, cancellation, and isolation MUST remain unchanged.
The README MUST explain configuration, support checks, pinning, and the cost/latency caveat. Effort is not a monetary budget or provider guarantee.


<a id="REQ-21"></a>

**REQ-21** Advisor command argument autocomplete

The registered advisor command MUST suggest show, model, reasoning, timeout, --global, and --project at its root.
Static choices MUST match a case-sensitive token prefix. Completion MUST preserve preceding arguments and whitespace, then append a space.
The grammar MUST accept one scope flag before, between, or after settings arguments. Repeated or conflicting scopes MUST receive no suggestions.
Model suggestions MUST use current available physical chat entries, not virtual entries or remote catalog refreshes.
Provider identifiers MUST be distinct and sorted. Provider matching MUST use a case-insensitive prefix.
Model matching MUST use Pi fuzzyFilter across identifiers and display names within the completed provider. Invalid settings identifiers MUST be excluded.
Reasoning suggestions MUST use fresh settings and advertised support for the selection targeted by the save scope.
Omitted scope and --global MUST use the global selection. Trusted --project MUST use the effective selection, including global fallback.
The extension MUST NOT read untrusted project settings. Missing context, missing models, invalid syntax, excess arguments, and failed lookups MUST return no dynamic suggestions.
Static suggestions MUST remain available without settings or catalogs. Lookup failures MUST remain silent without notifications or retries.
Session start and tree navigation MUST replace completion context. Shutdown MUST clear it. A context revision MUST reject pending old-context results.
Completion MUST NOT save settings, change the parent model, invoke tools, or generate. It MUST NOT add a dependency on pi-magic8ball.
The README MUST distinguish registered completion behavior from the known Pi 1.0.4 command-name Tab routing limitation.


## Host integration and results {#integration}

<a id="REQ-8"></a>

**REQ-8** Structured tool results

The package MUST register exactly advisor, advisor_sessions, and advisor_close as model-only tools. Each MUST define strict input and output schemas.
Successful advisor results MUST carry ok, advisory: true, session, response, turns, model, per-call usage, and cumulative consultation usage.
The extension, not the advisor model, MUST construct the structured tool result. The response field MUST carry unstructured advice as defined by REQ-17.
REQ-12 defines usage completeness fields and failure totals.
Failure results MUST carry ok: false, error: {code,message}, and per-call usage. REQ-11 defines additional limit details.
Existing session identifiers MUST accompany continuation failures.
Tool content, details, and structuredContent MUST agree. Failures MUST set isError. Host usage MUST contain only this call's usage, not cumulative usage.
The tool guidance MUST tell the main agent to explain objective, understanding, evidence, constraints, and uncertainty. It MUST prohibit citing advice as evidence or permission.
It MUST recommend continuation for the same issue and disclose provider charges. The extension MUST NOT automatically execute advice or continue consultations.


<a id="REQ-9"></a>

**REQ-9** Standalone package and verification

The package MUST load through Pi's resource loader without model work. Loading MUST NOT change profile settings or start background resources.
Runtime Pi and TypeBox packages MUST remain host-provided optional wildcard peers. pi-magic8ball MUST NOT be a dependency.
The package MUST provide repeatable Node test and TypeScript check commands. Acceptance tests MUST use injected mock responses and temporary configuration directories.
The README MUST describe loading, model setup, multi-turn use, close, limits, ephemeral state, transcript retention caveats, and advisory responsibility.
Paid provider checks MUST require separate authorization. Offline checks MUST NOT claim model reasoning quality or provider interoperability.


<a id="REQ-11"></a>

**REQ-11** Resource-specific limit diagnostics

On a resource limit failure, the extension MUST retain error.code = limit-exceeded.
It MUST add error.limit = {resource, maximum, actual} with nonnegative integer measurements.
resource MUST be input-bytes, reply-bytes, history-bytes, turns, or sessions.
maximum MUST be the inclusive local bound. actual MUST be the measured bytes or attempted pair/session count.
The extension MUST use fixed messages that identify the resource and its recovery action.
Input errors MUST ask for a shorter message. Reply errors MUST ask for a shorter requested answer.
History and turn errors MUST ask for a new consultation with an explicit summary. Session errors MUST ask to close idle consultations.
Diagnostics MUST NOT include message contents or raw provider errors. All REQ-4 bounds and rollback behavior MUST remain unchanged.


<a id="REQ-12"></a>

**REQ-12** Reported usage and completeness

Every advisor success or failure MUST include usageComplete, a boolean for this call's reported usage.
It MUST be true if no completion attempt began or a completed response supplied usage before return.
It MUST be false if a completion attempt began but no usage-bearing response was observed before return.
An exception, cancellation, or timeout after that attempt MUST NOT imply zero remote cost or completed remote cancellation.
Completed rejected replies MUST retain their reported usage and usageComplete = true.
Every successful consultation MUST retain totalUsageComplete, initially true, alongside known cumulative usage.
An attempt with usageComplete = false MUST make totalUsageComplete false for the rest of that consultation.
Successful results MUST return totalUsage and totalUsageComplete. Failures MUST return both when their requested consultation still exists.
Busy failures MUST mark cumulative usage incomplete while the other request is pending, without changing stored accounting.
A pending request MUST NOT add estimated usage. Late responses MUST NOT change state or repair incomplete totals.
Totals MUST be independent snapshots. Host usage MUST remain per-call only.
Completeness describes locally observed reporting, not verified provider billing or a monetary guarantee.


<a id="REQ-13"></a>

**REQ-13** Session capacity and known usage

Each advisor_sessions entry MUST include totalUsage, totalUsageComplete, turnsRemaining, historyBytes, and historyBytesRemaining.
Usage MUST be the known cumulative snapshot defined by REQ-12. A pending completion attempt MUST mark that snapshot incomplete.
Capacity MUST count only committed history. historyBytes MUST use the serialized UTF-8 calculation in REQ-4.
turnsRemaining MUST equal 24 minus committed pairs. historyBytesRemaining MUST equal 49152 minus committed history bytes.
The manager's injected test limits MAY replace those constants for offline boundary tests.
Returned nested objects MUST NOT expose mutable manager state. Metadata MUST NOT add full messages, advice, thinking, or token estimates.
Discovery MUST NOT run a model, change accounting, or alter consultation history.


<a id="REQ-14"></a>

**REQ-14** Safe tool presentation and progress

The extension MUST register call and result renderers for all three tools.
Advisor results MUST show an advisory label, session, and known per-call usage. REQ-19 defines collapsed previews and full expanded advice.
No renderer MUST infer a status from advice.
Expanded results MUST additionally show model, turns, and known cumulative usage with completeness labels.
Failures MUST show safe diagnostics and label incomplete usage. Missing details MUST use fixed fallback text, not raw result content.
Discovery and close renderers MUST show metadata and close outcomes without reconstructing transcripts.
Renderers MUST neutralize data control characters, fit terminal widths, and use the current callback theme.
The advisor tool MUST emit phase-only updates: preparing before new-model preparation and waiting before a completion attempt.
Updates MUST NOT contain advice, thinking, explicit input, raw errors, or usage. Callback errors MUST NOT change the consultation outcome.
No update MUST occur for invalid arguments or exhausted capacity. No late completion MUST emit updates.
Final model-facing JSON and structuredContent MUST remain identical. Rendering MUST NOT change data or start provider work.


<a id="REQ-15"></a>

**REQ-15** Opt-in live verification procedure

The README MUST provide an opt-in procedure for one successful consultation and one continuation against a designated physical model.
The procedure MUST require separate spending authorization before either call. It MUST disclose the absence of a local monetary cap.
It MUST limit the run to two requests, forbid automatic retries, and stop after any failure.
It MUST use nonsecret text, verify model pinning and reported usage, and close the consultation.
It MUST identify provider/model, Pi/Node versions, outcomes, and usage completeness in a report without storing credentials.
Offline checks MUST NOT invoke that procedure or claim live interoperability. This task MUST NOT perform live calls without further authorization.


<a id="REQ-16"></a>

**REQ-16** Safe reply rejection diagnostics

For invalid-response, the extension MUST identify the failed validation in error.message using fixed text. It MUST NOT expose reply text, thinking, raw provider errors, or provider-supplied field values. Default calls MUST NOT add result fields; REQ-22 defines the opt-in diagnostic fields.
Validation MUST check in order: provider error/abort, normal stop, content shape, reply byte limit, and nonblank text. REQ-17 removes marker validation.
Content MUST be an array of nonnull text or thinking blocks. Every text block MUST have string text. Malformed content MUST return invalid-response rather than provider-failed.
Messages MUST distinguish abnormal completion, unsupported or malformed content, and absent text. Every rejection message MUST state that no exchange was committed.
The extension MUST preserve byte limits, known usage, rollback, and no retry. It MUST NOT infer which validation failed in an earlier call whose reply is unavailable.


<a id="REQ-18"></a>

**REQ-18** Responses visible without expansion

REQ-19 supersedes the former requirement for full advice in the collapsed view. Wrapping and control neutralization MUST remain as defined in REQ-14.
The expanded view MUST show full advice and metadata. The README MUST describe the current behavior.
Showing advice MUST use the existing tool result and renderer. The extension MUST NOT send duplicate custom/user messages, add transcript entries, start parent model turns, or change result content/details/structuredContent for this presentation change.
Partial or failed replies MUST NOT appear as successful advice. Existing privacy, completion validation, lifecycle, and provider-call behavior MUST remain unchanged.


<a id="REQ-22"></a>

**REQ-22** Opt-in privacy-safe failure diagnostics

The advisor input MAY contain diagnostics, a boolean. Omission and false MUST preserve the previous failure envelope. Null and nonboolean values MUST fail validation. True MUST add error.diagnostics to failures of that call only; successes MUST remain unchanged. This extends REQ-1 and REQ-8 without relaxing unknown-field validation. REQ-16's prohibition on additional fields remains applicable to default calls; opted-in failures MAY add only this diagnostic object.
Diagnostics MUST contain phase: validation, preparation, completion, response-validation, or commit. Validation covers input, reservation, and history preflight. Preparation covers selection resolution. Completion covers the completion invocation until a response is returned. Response-validation covers returned usage, reply validation, and full-pair history bounds. Commit covers final cancellation/deadline checks and committing the pair.
Diagnostics MUST contain category: advisor-error for extension-defined errors, local-error for unexpected exceptions outside completion, or unknown for unclassified completion exceptions. A returned error or aborted stop reason MUST use provider-error or provider-aborted respectively, except for the terminal error hints in REQ-23. Terminal abort MUST take precedence over error hints.
For thrown completion exceptions, the extension MUST read only own data descriptors for status and code. Status 401/403 MUST map to authentication; 400/404/409/413/422 to provider-rejection; 429 to rate-limit; 408/500/502/503/504 to transport. Recognized status MUST take precedence over code. Codes ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, ENOTFOUND, and EAI_AGAIN MUST map to transport when status is unrecognized. All other values, accessor fields, and descriptor inspection failures MUST yield unknown. The extension MUST NOT parse free-form provider error messages, except for the fixed SDK wrapper in REQ-23. It MUST NOT traverse causes, headers, or payloads.
When a selection is known, diagnostics MUST include model with configured reasoning and selectionSource: global, project, or unknown. Preparation MUST report resolved settings before checking model availability/authentication. A continuation MUST use the pinned model and original source, not current settings. Unresolved selection MUST omit both fields. Late preparation/completion MUST NOT mutate returned diagnostics or pinned state.
Diagnostic categories are hints, not verified root causes. Errors MUST retain existing fixed codes/messages, usage completeness, rollback, isolation, and no-retry behavior. Diagnostics MUST NOT expose credentials, headers, exception text, rejected advice, thinking, or arbitrary provider payloads. Renderers MUST display opted-in diagnostics with existing width/control protections. The README MUST explain opt-in, phases, categories, selection provenance, transcript persistence, and the zero-usage billing caveat. Enabling diagnostics MUST NOT authorize another live request.


<a id="REQ-23"></a>

**REQ-23** Integer timeouts and safe SDK terminal error hints

For each completion attempt, advisor MUST pass timeoutMs = max(1, floor(deadline milliseconds minus elapsed milliseconds)).
The timeout MUST remain an integer within the original per-call deadline budget. The local deadline and cancellation checks MUST remain unchanged.
For opted-in diagnostics on a terminal error, advisor MUST inspect only an own data descriptor for errorMessage.
It MUST NOT invoke getters. Missing, nonstring, or hostile metadata MUST retain provider-error without extra fields.
An exact errorMessage of "timeout must be an integer" or "timeout must be a positive integer" MUST report category sdk-error and code sdk-invalid-timeout.
The renderer MUST show fixed text that identifies the SDK timeout constraint.
Otherwise, advisor MUST check only the SDK wrapper prefix "<selected-provider> API error (<status>): ", except for the fixed rejection detail in REQ-24.
For provider openai, the wrapper label MUST be OpenAI. Status MUST be exactly three decimal digits from 400 through 599.
A matching wrapper MUST add httpStatus and use REQ-22's HTTP category mapping. Unmapped statuses MUST retain provider-error.
No body, free-form message, credential, header, advice, or thinking MUST enter diagnostic output.
These text-derived hints MUST NOT claim a verified remote root cause. Terminal abort MUST remain provider-aborted without text-derived hints.
Default failure envelopes and successful envelopes MUST remain unchanged. Opt-in, usage reporting, rollback, isolation, and no retry MUST remain unchanged.
Tests MUST exercise the installed OpenAI Responses adapter with a mock fetch and a synthetic key. They MUST make no network requests.


<a id="REQ-24"></a>

**REQ-24** Tool-free xAI requests and fixed rejection diagnostics

REQ-25 supersedes the provider-specific toolChoice rules. Advisor MUST continue to declare zero tools and reject tool-call replies.
The selected model, effort, timeout, token bound, and no-retry options MUST remain unchanged.
For opted-in xai terminal errors with the exact SDK HTTP 400 wrapper, advisor MUST recognize these complete rejection details:
- Invalid request content: A tool_choice was set on the request but no tools were specified.
- A tool_choice was set on the request but no tools were specified.
- 400 Invalid request content: A tool_choice was set on the request but no tools were specified.
For an exact match, diagnostics MUST add code tool-choice-without-tools to the existing provider-rejection category and httpStatus 400.
The renderer MUST show fixed text that identifies tool_choice without tools. It MUST NOT expose the original detail.
Arbitrary details, partial matches, appended content, different providers, and different statuses MUST retain existing hints without this code.
Default failures, successes, isolation, usage, rollback, and no retries MUST remain unchanged. No settings or credential files MUST change.


<a id="REQ-25"></a>

**REQ-25** Provider-neutral tool-free request options

For every creation and continuation request, advisor MUST omit the toolChoice option from the host model-registry call.
This rule MUST apply to every selected provider, including custom providers. Advisor MUST NOT select toolChoice behavior by provider identifier.
Pi MUST control provider payload construction. Advisor MUST continue to declare zero tools and reject tool-call replies.
The selected model, configured effort, integer timeout, cancellation signal, token bound, cache retention, session identifier, and disabled retries MUST remain unchanged.
Private diagnostics, atomic history, usage accounting, settings, and authentication MUST remain unchanged.
This requirement supersedes only REQ-24's provider-specific toolChoice rules.


- #REQ-25 supersedes: [#REQ-24](#REQ-24)


<a id="REQ-26"></a>

**REQ-26** Configurable pinned advisor deadline

Advisor MUST use a default deadline of 300000 milliseconds per call. The user approved this five-minute default.
Settings MAY contain root timeoutMs as an integer from 1 through 2147483647 milliseconds, inclusive.
The upper bound MUST match Node's timer range. Zero, negative, fractional, nonnumber, null, and larger values MUST fail settings validation.
Timeout MUST resolve independently of model selection: trusted project timeoutMs, then global timeoutMs, then the default.
A project model without timeoutMs MUST inherit the global timeout. A timeout-only project MUST retain the global model.
Untrusted project settings MUST remain unread. Invalid global settings MUST fail even when a project overrides them.

Each new consultation MUST pin the resolved timeout with its model. Configuration changes MUST affect new consultations only.
Every call MUST measure its budget from call entry, including preparation. The SDK MUST receive a positive integer remaining timeout.
Before settings resolve, preparation MUST use the default deadline. A constructor test override MAY replace that initial default.
When settings resolve, advisor MUST rearm the deadline from the original call-entry time, not start a new budget.
If the configured budget has already elapsed, advisor MUST fail with timeout before generation.
Late preparation callbacks MUST NOT change deadlines, diagnostics, state, or schedule timers after return or cancellation.
Cancellation, disabled retries, rollback, usage completeness, and rejection of late commits MUST remain unchanged.

The user-only command timeout without a value MUST show effective milliseconds and source without writes or generation.
The timeout <milliseconds> command MUST accept only decimal integer text within the settings range.
The timeout default command MUST remove only that scope's explicit timeout, restoring inheritance or the default.
Timeout commands MUST work without a configured model. They MUST preserve the scope's own model and reasoning, without copying another scope's model.
Model, picker, and reasoning saves MUST preserve the target scope's explicit timeout, without copying an inherited timeout into that scope.
Preserved fields MUST come from the target layer at the save checkpoint under the exclusive lock, not an earlier command snapshot.
Reset MAY atomically save an empty settings object. Existing lock, trust, file bounds, and checkpoint safety rules MUST remain unchanged.
show MUST include effective timeout and source. Autocomplete MUST add timeout and timeout default without settings reads or provider work.
Tool inputs MUST NOT accept caller-supplied timeouts. Existing tool result schemas and model metadata MUST remain unchanged.
The README MUST document units, range, precedence, pinning, reset, and the fact that a longer deadline is not a billing guarantee.


<a id="REQ-27"></a>

**REQ-27** Short provider prompt caching

For every creation and continuation request, advisor MUST set cacheRetention to short at the host model-registry boundary.
Advisor MUST retain one stable sessionId per consultation. Different consultations MUST use different identifiers, independent of the parent session.
Advisor MUST retain the fixed system prompt and append-only validated exchange text. It MUST NOT add changing cache metadata to the prompt.
Pi MUST control provider cache payload construction. Advisor MUST NOT add provider-specific cache fields or a new cache setting.
Cache support, minimum prompt size, lifetime, and cache hits depend on the provider. Short MUST NOT imply guaranteed savings or erasure.
Closing a consultation MUST remove local state only. It MUST NOT claim to delete provider caches or the parent transcript.
Model and effort pinning, zero tools, retries, timeout, cancellation, rollback, and usage reporting MUST remain unchanged.
The README MUST describe short caching, same-session continuation, provider-dependent results, and the limits of local close.
This requirement supersedes only REQ-25's instruction to preserve cache retention.


- #REQ-27 supersedes: [#REQ-25](#REQ-25)


<a id="REQ-28"></a>

**REQ-28** Private opaque continuation state

After reply validation, advisor MUST preserve allowlisted opaque replay data for the pinned provider, model, and API only.
Supported APIs MUST be openai-responses, openai-codex-responses, azure-openai-responses, google-generative-ai, google-vertex, anthropic-messages, and bedrock-converse-stream.
For Responses APIs, replay MUST preserve encrypted_content and reasoning item IDs. It MUST remove plaintext reasoning content and summaries.
Responses reasoning signatures MUST contain type reasoning, a nonempty string ID, and nonempty string encrypted_content. Replay summary MUST be empty.
Replay MAY retain status only when it is completed, incomplete, or in_progress. Other reasoning-item fields MUST NOT survive.
Responses text signatures MUST retain only version 1, a string ID, and commentary or final_answer phase when present.
For Google APIs, replay MUST preserve valid base64 text/thinking signatures on their original blocks. Replayed thinking text MUST be empty.
For Anthropic and Bedrock, replay MUST preserve only redacted thinking with a nonempty string signature. Ordinary signed plaintext thinking MUST NOT survive.
All supported APIs MUST preserve original text-block boundaries and order. Absent, malformed, and unsupported metadata MUST be omitted without changing valid reply text.
A reply with a different provider or model MUST NOT contribute replay data. Unsupported APIs MUST keep the existing text-only history behavior.

Opaque replay MUST remain process-local and private. Results, metadata, progress, renderers, diagnostics, parent tool results, and persisted files MUST NOT contain replay data.
The extension MUST NOT retain plaintext thinking, summaries, raw provider replies, arbitrary metadata, or response IDs for server-side chaining.
Advisor MUST NOT enable server-side storage or previous_response_id. Pi MUST continue to own provider payload construction.
Continuation contexts MUST use the original API identity and detached replay copies. Provider mutation MUST NOT change retained state.
Replay MUST commit atomically with its validated user/reply pair. Failure, cancellation, timeout, and late completion MUST leave prior replay unchanged.
Different consultations MUST NOT share replay data. Close and lifecycle clear MUST release local replay with the consultation.

The existing 49152-byte history limit MUST include private replay. Count UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify entries with role, text, and optional replay.
Each replay value MUST contain api and sanitized content. With no replay, the existing role/text byte measurement MUST remain unchanged.
Pending-user and full-pair checks MUST use this combined measurement. Overflow MUST fail with history-bytes and commit no pair or replay.
The README MUST describe opaque local state, combined byte accounting, supported formats, and the plaintext-thinking limitation.
This requirement supersedes only REQ-2's prohibition on retaining opaque thinking metadata and REQ-4's role/text-only byte formula.
Plaintext thinking exclusion, public advice text, isolation, short caching, request controls, usage, and failure behavior MUST remain unchanged.


- #REQ-28 supersedes: [#REQ-4](#REQ-4)


- #REQ-28 supersedes: [#REQ-2](#REQ-2)


<a id="REQ-29"></a>

**REQ-29** Model-sized advisor context

Advisor MUST replace the 49152-byte history cap with the pinned advisor model's contextWindow from Pi's model registry.
The resolved value MUST be a positive safe integer. Missing or invalid values MUST return model-unavailable before generation.
The model window MUST be pinned at creation. Parent model and parent context usage MUST NOT supply this value.
Each history entry MAY retain validated reply usage for context measurement. Raw replies and plaintext thinking MUST remain excluded.
Context tokens MUST follow Pi 1.0.4: latest positive validated assistant calculateContextTokens(usage), plus estimateTokens for later messages.
With no positive usage, advisor MUST estimate each message with Pi's public estimateTokens helper, including its fixed system prompt.
Opaque ciphertext length MUST NOT be treated as a token count. Context measurement is an estimate, not a tokenizer guarantee.
Before dispatch, estimated pending context plus the existing 4096-token output request MUST NOT exceed contextWindow.
After reply validation, estimated committed context MUST NOT exceed contextWindow. Equality MUST pass.
Overflow MUST return limit-exceeded with resource context-tokens, maximum contextWindow, and attempted token count.
Failed or interrupted pairs MUST NOT advance retained context. Completed rejected usage MUST still count toward cumulative usage.
Advisor MUST NOT trim, summarize, compact, retry, or request parent history automatically.
The 8-session, 24-pair, 16384-byte input/reply, timeout, and output request limits MUST remain unchanged.
Advisor success results and session metadata MUST expose contextUsage with tokens, contextWindow, and percent.
Failed advisor calls MUST include retained contextUsage when the consultation still exists with a resolved window.
Percent MUST equal 100 times tokens divided by contextWindow. Returned values MUST be detached snapshots.
Metadata MUST replace historyBytesRemaining with contextUsage. historyBytes MAY remain informational, without a fixed cap.
Strict schemas MUST reflect the new metadata and limit resource. Unsupported unknown fields MUST remain rejected.
This requirement supersedes only REQ-4 and REQ-28's retained-history byte cap and REQ-13's byte-remaining and no-token-estimate rules.


- #REQ-29 supersedes: [#REQ-13](#REQ-13)


- #REQ-29 supersedes: [#REQ-28](#REQ-28)


- #REQ-29 supersedes: [#REQ-4](#REQ-4)


<a id="REQ-30"></a>

**REQ-30** Visible advisor question and Pi-like usage line

The advisor call renderer MUST show the main agent's explicit message below the call heading, with original line breaks.
Display sanitization MUST neutralize terminal controls. Rendering MUST NOT change the message sent to the provider.
The full sanitized message MUST be visible. The renderer MUST NOT show hidden replay state, raw provider payloads, or plaintext thinking.
Phase updates MUST remain phase-only. No new transcript entries, provider calls, parent-footer replacement, or persisted consultation files are permitted.
Both collapsed and expanded advisor results MUST show a consultation-local usage line below the result heading.
The line MUST show cumulative uncached input with ↑, output with ↓, cache reads with R, and cache writes with W when nonzero.
CH MUST use the latest call's reported cacheRead divided by input plus cacheRead plus cacheWrite, times 100.
Unknown usage or a zero denominator MUST show CH?. Output tokens MUST NOT enter the denominator.
The line MUST show cumulative reported cost to three decimals and context percent/window from REQ-29.
Token abbreviations MUST follow Pi 1.0.4's footer thresholds. Context percent and CH MUST use one decimal.
Missing context from historic results MUST show ?/?. Incomplete cumulative usage MUST be labeled incomplete.
The line MUST NOT show sub or auto labels. Advice MUST NOT acquire a semantic status classification.
Known cumulative failures MUST show the line with retained context. Expanded session metadata MUST show context rather than remaining bytes.
Existing eight-row advice previews, expanded full advice, safe failures, current themes, width bounds, isolation, and opaque-state privacy MUST remain.
README MUST explain visible questions, model-sized estimated context, remaining limits, cumulative totals, per-call CH, and reported cost.


<a id="REQ-31"></a>

**REQ-31** Remove fixed consultation caps

Advisor MUST NOT cap active consultations, committed exchanges, message bytes, or reply bytes with fixed extension limits.
Advisor MUST omit maxTokens from every completion options object. Pi MUST control the model output allowance.
Before dispatch, advisor MUST compare estimated pending context tokens with the pinned model contextWindow, without a fixed output reserve.
After reply validation, advisor MUST compare estimated committed context tokens with that same window.
Equality MUST pass both checks. Overflow MUST return limit-exceeded with resource context-tokens and commit no exchange.
The fixed safe context error MUST report maximum contextWindow and actual estimated tokens.
Completed rejected replies MUST retain their known usage. A failed continuation MUST retain its previous context and replay.

Success and discovery schemas MUST permit exchange counts above 24. Discovery MUST permit more than eight entries.
Discovery MUST omit turnsRemaining. Session renderers MUST show committed exchange counts and all listed consultations, without a fixed eight-entry cutoff.
Public limit schemas MUST accept only context-tokens as a resource. Removed resource names MUST fail schema validation.
The README MUST describe the removed caps, Pi output defaults, retained context checks, and unchanged deadline.

The configurable timeout, caller cancellation, busy protection, no retries, strict inputs, reply validation, and isolation MUST remain unchanged.
Usage snapshots, opaque replay privacy, close, lifecycle reset, and ephemeral retention MUST remain unchanged.
The 16384-byte settings-file bound, 80-code-point labels, picker row bounds, and eight-row advice previews MUST remain unchanged.

This requirement supersedes REQ-4's fixed consultation, exchange, input-byte, reply-byte, and output-token bounds.
It supersedes REQ-11's removed limit resources and REQ-13's turnsRemaining field.
It supersedes REQ-29's fixed output reserve and preservation of the removed caps.
Earlier requirements and acceptance criteria MUST NOT restore these caps through a preservation clause.

Mocks use synthetic keys and provider state. They establish local payload construction and privacy/resource invariants, not live cache-hit improvement, provider acceptance, savings, billing, or remote deletion.
Responses replay is allowlisted and sanitized. Google retains only valid base64 thought signatures with empty thinking text. Anthropic and Bedrock retain only opaque redacted thinking. Ordinary signed plaintext thinking remains unsupported when a provider requires it for continuation or caching.
Private state counts against the existing 49152-byte limit; text blocks are duplicated in the private replay representation, so supported formats can reach the limit sooner.
A further live probe requires separate spending authorization and a reload. No new paid provider request, live setting change, commit, push, or deployment occurred during this fix. Existing worktree changes were preserved.
